<div class="accordion-item">
<h2 class="accordion-header" id="headingTec">
<button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#collapseTec" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="collapseTec">
<strong>⚙️ Technology</strong>
</button>
</h2>
<div id="collapseTec" class="accordion-collapse collapse" aria-labelledby="headingTec" data-bs-parent="#competenciasAccordion">
<div class="accordion-body">

**[Technology](https://xtec.gencat.cat/web/.content/curriculum/eso/curriculum-175-2022/Tecnologia.pdf "Technology"){target="_blank"}**

The subject of Technology contributes to responding to the needs of citizens in the face of the technological challenges posed by today's society, especially the growing digitization. Thus, this subject serves as a basis, not only for understanding social evolution, but also for being able to act with technical, scientific and ethical criteria in the exercise of responsible and active citizenship, using the generation of knowledge as a driver of development and encouraging the participation of students on an equal footing with a comprehensive vision of technology, highlighting its social aspect.

The challenges of the 21st century are considered in detail and developed in depth in this subject. In this way, economic, social and environmental aspects related to the influence of technological development, and of automation and robotization, are addressed, both in terms of the organization of work, as in other areas of society, with an approach that promotes equal treatment and the rejection of attitudes of discrimination based on gender or other factors. Likewise, sustainability is closely linked to the manufacturing processes, the correct selection of materials and handling techniques and the control systems that allow resources to be optimized. In this sense, technology provides essential means to address sustainable development goals such as universal access to energy and communication, as well as education, food and health among others.

The interdisciplinary nature of the subject contributes to the overall achievement of the stage objectives and the achievement of the Competency Profile. Technical aspects related to mathematical competence and competences in science, technology and engineering, digital competence, as well as other transversal knowledge associated with linguistic competence, multilingual competence, personal, social and learning to learn competence, entrepreneurial competence, citizen competence and competence in awareness and cultural expressions are developed.

The specific skills are closely related to the backbones on which the subject is based. Some of the essential elements that make up this subject are the transversal nature of technology, the impetus for collaboration and teamwork, computational thinking and its implications in automation and the connection of devices to the Internet, as well as the promotion of attitudes such as creativity, perseverance, responsibility in sustainable technological development or entrepreneurship incorporating digital technologies. It is also worth noting the eminently functional nature of interdisciplinary problem solving and project planning, which constitutes the main backbone of the subject and reflects its competence approach.

The skills must be worked on in the context of learning situations, connected to reality and which invite students to reflection, collaboration and action.

The achievement of the specific skills constitutes the basis for the student's competence assessment and will be assessed through the assessment criteria. There is no unequivocal and direct link between assessment criteria and knowledge, specific skills will be assessed through the implementation of different knowledge, providing the necessary flexibility to establish connections between them.

Approaching a competence approach, the evaluation criteria and knowledge, graduated through the cycles, are structured around specific competences. This progression, which starts from very close and manipulative environments connecting with the stages of infant and primary education, facilitates the transition towards more formal learning and favors the development of the ability to think abstractly.

The assessment criteria, as they explain the assessment of the skills and knowledge that needs to be developed, specify the learning we want to identify in the students and the way to do it. They are directly linked to specific skills. The assessment criteria make it possible to measure the degree of development of these skills and the teacher can flexibly connect them with the knowledge of the area or the subject during the teaching-learning process.

The teaching staff must contextualize and make these criteria more flexible in accordance with the circumstances of their activity. Their character is markedly competitive and makes them evaluators of both the capabilities deployed and the different types of knowledge, that is, knowledge, skills, values ​​and attitudes that students must acquire in order to develop in multiple situations typical of modern society.

At the primary education stage, students already start developing design and computational thinking projects. In the compulsory secondary education stage, this subject allows, on the one hand, to give continuity to the Technology and Digitization subject of previous courses and, on the other, to deepen the achievement of skills, as well as to prepare and foster in students an entrepreneurial attitude towards further studies or the performance of professional activities.

The subject is organized into four interrelated blocks of knowledge: *problem and project solving process;* *technological operators;* *computational thinking, automation and robotics,* and *sustainable technology*.

The implementation of the blog *problem solving process and projects*, through strategies and methodologies for learning based on the development of projects, incorporates current techniques adapted from the business and industrial world, in accordance with educational trends in other countries. While great importance is given to the phases of research, ideation, design and manufacture, an adequate treatment of the phase of presentation and communication of results is also included, as a key aspect for the dissemination of the work carried out.

The blog *technological operators*, applied to projects, offers an insight into the mechanical and electronic elements that allow solving problems using digital control techniques in real situations.

The block *computational thinking, automation and robotics* lays the foundations, not only for understanding, but also for knowing how to design and implement programmed control systems, as well as programming computers or mobile devices. The incorporation of artificial intelligence modules and data engineering techniques offer added value here. Along these same lines, the integration of telecommunications in control systems opens the door to the Internet of Things and allows its use in practical applications and can respond to personal or collective needs.

The *sustainable technology* blog addresses the knowledge and application of sustainability criteria in the use of materials, process design and, in energy matters, recognizing the importance of personal, social and cultural diversity and influencing issues such as open learning communities and community services with an active commitment both locally and globally.

All this is considered in the last year of the compulsory education stage from a competence and eminently practical perspective, based on the idea of ​​learning by doing. This idea consists of providing an environment so that students have the opportunity to carry out certain tasks while exploring, discovering, experimenting, applying and reflecting on what they do. The proposal of learning situations developed in a manufacturing laboratory, understood as a space to materialize interdisciplinary projects with a competent and practical approach, which allows the incorporation of work techniques, rapid prototyping and offline manufacturing with 3D printing systems and other digital manufacturing tools, favors the involvement of students in their learning process which will therefore be more meaningful and lasting.

In this sense, it is convenient to keep in mind that the development of technological projects is a very suitable option as a structuring element of knowledge in the field of Technology.

In the Technology subject, a total of 6 specific skills are worked on, which are the concretization of the operational indicators of the key skills defined in the students' exit skill profile at the end of basic education.

**Specific competence 1**

**Identify and propose technological problems with initiative and creativity, while studying the needs of the immediate environment, applying strategies and collaborative and iterative processes related to projects, to devise and plan solutions in an efficient and innovative way.**

**Evaluation criteria**

1.1 Ideate and plan entrepreneurial technological solutions that generate value for the community, based on the observation and analysis of the immediate environment, while studying the needs, requirements and possibilities for improvement.

1.2 Apply, with initiative, collaborative project management strategies with an interdisciplinary perspective, following an iterative validation process, from the ideation phase to problem solving.

1.3 Develop project management in a creative way, applying strategies and collaborative techniques, as well as research methods for the ideation of efficient, innovative and environmentally friendly solutions.

This competence starts from the search and analysis of the needs of the immediate environment (centre, neighbourhood, locality, region...) to detect and address the problems that can be solved through technology which, subsequently and after their analysis, will be the basis of the problem-solving process, providing solutions to the detected needs. Included in this competence are aspects related to ideation, design and the search for solutions through methodologies close to scientific research, investigation techniques, planning and task management following the phases of a technological project, and strategies are incorporated to introduce students to the management of cooperative and iterative projects for continuous improvement of the solution.

In this competition, various techniques are also addressed to train and enhance creativity with the aim of making it more efficient. The entrepreneurial spirit is also encouraged from an approach that includes the leadership and coordination of work teams, with a global vision and a co-educational treatment, guaranteeing the development of the initiative and proactivity of all students.

**Specific competence 2**

**Apply different techniques and interdisciplinary knowledge using technological procedures and resources while anticipating the life cycle of products to build sustainable technological solutions that respond to identified needs.**

**Evaluation criteria**

2.1 Analyze the design of a product that responds to a perceived need, evaluating its demand, evolution and end-of-life forecast with ethical, sustainable and responsible criteria.

2.2 Manufacture technological products and solutions, making use of assisted design, using the different manual, mechanical and digital production techniques, using appropriately the different mechanical, electrical, electronic and digital materials and resources.

2.3 Argue the technological solutions brought to the needs raised, assessing their economic feasibility, functional, sustainable and efficient use.

This competence refers both to the process of manufacturing products or developing systems that provide solutions both to problems raised and to the actions involved in this process. The techniques and procedures necessary for the construction and creation of technological products or systems are addressed, including both manual manufacturing and manufacturing using computer-assisted technologies. In this way, the aim is to develop the skills necessary for the design and creation of products, encouraging the application of digital manufacturing techniques and the use of technological resources. The different actions that are unleashed in the creative process involve the intervention of knowledge specific to this subject (mechanical, electrical and electronic operators), which are integrated with others, thus contributing to a learning competence in which different areas intervene.

In addition, reference is made to the study of the phases of the product's life cycle, analyzing the characteristics and conditions of the process that could improve the final result, making it more sustainable and efficient. They include, for example, aspects related to the energy consumption of the manufacturing process, obsolescence, cycles of use or the environmental repercussions of both the manufacture of the product and its use or removal from the cycle, encouraging eco-socially responsible attitudes and habits in the use and creation of products.

**Specific competence 3**

**Communicate, argue and disseminate technological ideas and solutions in different virtual spaces, using various resources while applying the elements and techniques necessary to exchange information and encourage teamwork.**

**Evaluation criteria**

3.1 Exchange information and encourage teamwork in an assertive way, using digital tools, technical vocabulary, symbols and diagrams of appropriate technological systems.

3.2 Present and disseminate technological proposals or solutions in a concrete way, using intonation, expression, adaptation of speech and time, using an inclusive language free of sexist stereotypes.

This competence covers aspects necessary to communicate, express and disseminate ideas, proposals and opinions in a clear and fluid manner in various contexts, media and channels. Reference is made to the proper use of language and the incorporation of the technical terminology required in the process of designing and creating technological solutions. In this sense, aspects necessary for effective communication are addressed (for example, assertiveness, adequate management of exposure time, good expression, intonation, adaptation to the context, use of inclusive and non-sexist language...) as well as other aspects related to the use of digital tools to disseminate and share resources, documents and information in different formats.

The need to exchange information with other people implies a responsible and respectful attitude towards the work team, as well as towards the protocols established in collaborative work, applicable both in the personal context and to interactions in the network through digital tools, virtual platforms or social communication networks.

**Specific competence 4**

**Develop sustainable solutions to proposed problems that incorporate automation and emerging technologies, to design and build programmable and robotic control systems.**

**Evaluation criteria**

4.1 Design, build, control and/or simulate programmable automatic systems and robots that are capable of doing tasks autonomously, applying knowledge of mechanics, electronics, pneumatics and components of control systems, as well as other interdisciplinary knowledge.

4.2 Integrate into machines and technological systems emerging digital control and simulation applications such as the Internet of Things, massive data processing (*big data*) and artificial intelligence with a critical, ethical and sustainable sense.

This competence refers to the application of scientific-technological knowledge and the principles of computational thinking in the process of designing, simulating or building systems capable of performing functions autonomously. On the one hand, it involves actions aimed at the modeling and dimensioning of automatic or robotic systems that allow the incorporation of task automation: selection of suitable materials, the implementation of the technological system that underpins the operation of the machine and the design and dimensioning of its electromechanical elements. On the other hand, aspects related to the implementation of suitable algorithms for the automatic control of machines or the development of computer applications that solve a specific problem in various devices are included: computers, mobile devices and boards with microcontrollers.

Communication and interaction with objects are aspects closely linked to the control of technological processes or systems. In this sense, initiation into emerging technologies such as the Internet of Things, massive data processing (*Big Data*), artificial intelligence (AI) and the incorporation of these and other methodologies focused on the automation of processes in technological systems of different types with a critical and ethical sense must be considered.

**Specific competence 5**

**Use digital design and manufacturing tools, adapting and configuring them to needs while applying interdisciplinary knowledge, for a more efficient and sustainable production.**

**Evaluation criteria**

5.1 Solve proposed tasks efficiently through the use and configuration of different applications and digital tools, while applying interdisciplinary knowledge autonomously.

5.2 Use in the design of solutions, three-dimensional representation tools and virtual experimentation through simulators, for the construction of technological knowledge.

5.3 Use different presentation managers, tools for dissemination or publication of information to carry out collaborative tasks.

5.4 Set up programs or computer applications for the control of different automatisms.

The integration of digital technology in many situations is a reality and, in this sense, it is essential in the lifelong learning process. The competence addresses the incorporation of tools and digital devices in the different phases of the process, for example: the use of 3D design tools or experimentation through simulators in the design of solutions, the application of CAM/CAE technologies in the manufacture of products, the use of presentation managers or dissemination tools in the communication or publication of information, the development of computer programs or applications in the control of systems, the good use of collaboration tools in group work, etc. In each phase of the process, the application of digital technology is necessary to improve the results.

Additionally, this competence focuses on the responsible and efficient use of digital technology applied to the learning process. All this implies knowledge and understanding of the operation of the devices and applications used, allowing them to be adapted to personal needs. It is about taking advantage, on the one hand, of the diversity of possibilities offered by digital technology and, on the other, the contributions of interdisciplinary knowledge to improve the solutions provided.

**Specific competence 6**

**Analyze technological processes, assessing the impact on society and the environment, while applying sustainability criteria, to make an ethical and ecosocially responsible use of technology.**

**Evaluation criteria**

6.1 Make responsible use of technology, through the analysis and application of sustainability criteria in the selection of materials, design and manufacturing processes of technological products, while minimizing the impact on society and the planet.

6.2 Analyze the benefits and value the contribution of technologies to sustainable development and care for the environment, which are provided by bioclimatic architecture, renewable energies and efficient mobility.

6.3 Identify and assess the impact and benefits of the development of technological projects of a social nature through open communities, volunteer actions or community service projects.

Technology has responded to human needs throughout history by improving people's living conditions, but in turn having a negative impact on some aspects such as the environment. This competence includes the necessary analysis of the determining sustainability criteria in the design and manufacture of products and systems through the study of energy consumption, environmental pollution and eco-social impact. In addition, it is intended to show the activity of certain work teams on the Internet and the repercussion that some social projects can have through open communities, volunteer actions or community service projects, as well as the effect of the selection of materials, the mechanical system or the choice of energy sources and their conversions.

The aim is to promote technological development to improve social well-being by minimizing the repercussions in other areas, mentioned above. For this, all the criteria must be kept in mind from the initial moment of detection of the need and estimated in each of the phases of the creative process. In this sense, these issues are applied to the design of bioclimatic architecture in buildings and sustainable means of transport. Finally, attitudinal aspects related to the assessment of energy saving for the benefit of the environment and the contribution of emerging technologies, currently applicable in any field, to the achievement of sustainable development objectives are addressed.

**Knows**

The knowledge is formulated in relation to contexts where their learning skills can be developed. Teachers can incorporate alternative contexts if they consider it relevant.

In order to facilitate learning and the development of the corresponding specific skills, teachers can assess the possibility of organizing the knowledge of the subject, or of the different subjects coordinated in an area, based on situations.

The situations make it possible to program the course of any level, subject or area from a collection or sequence of challenges, contexts, circumstances of the real world, from which derive questions that need to be answered and that intertwine knowledge, that is, knowledge, skills, values ​​and attitudes with the capacities that support the competence approach to learning. This modifies the usual planning for the acquisition of knowledge and skills based on the academic logic specific to the areas of knowledge or subjects, embodied in the traditional sequence of disciplinary subjects. It aims to approach the learner's logic to give meaning to their learning based on the sequence of relevant contexts embodied in the situations.

**Problem and project resolution process**

- Strategies and techniques
- Application of collaborative project management strategies and iterative problem solving techniques.
- Search, comparison and study of the needs of the educational center, local and regional areas, etc. for the planning of collaborative or cooperative projects.
- Implementation of different ideation techniques for problem solving.
- Solving problems with an entrepreneurial, creative and persevering attitude, from an interdisciplinary perspective of technological activity, while promoting satisfaction and interest in the work and its quality.
- Products and materials
- Selection and use of different products and materials for solving problems.
- Analysis of the life cycle of a product and identification of the different phases.
- Selection of materials while using various strategies, according to their properties or requirements, for the resolution of problems and projects.
- Manufacturing
- Assessment, selection and use of different manufacturing techniques in solving problems and projects.
- Use of different design and computer-aided manufacturing tools in 2D and 3D, for the representation and/or manufacture of parts applied to projects.
- Assessment, selection and use of different manual and mechanical manufacturing techniques, in practical applications.
- Implementation, in practical applications, of digital manufacturing techniques, such as 3D printing and cutting.
- Diffusion
- Documentation, presentation and dissemination of projects, integrating different elements, techniques and tools. Use of effective communication based on intonation, expression, time management and adaptation of the speech and with the use of inclusive language free of gender stereotypes.

**Tech operators**

- Identification of basic analog electronic components and their symbology, with the analysis and physical and simulated assembly of elementary circuits.
- Representation, analysis, design, simulation and assembly of simple digital electronic circuits and their application.
- Representation, analysis, design, simulation and assembly of basic pneumatic circuits with components that fulfill a certain function in a mechanism or machine.
- Analysis, description and relationship of the different mechanical, electronic and pneumatic elements applied to robotics, using physical or simulated assembly.

**Computational thinking, automation and robotics**

- Use of different components of programmed control systems: controllers, sensors and actuators, which allow the optimization of resources and apply automation and robotization.
- Design and implementation of IT applications for computers and mobile devices. Use of computer simulators in the verification and verification of the operation of the designed systems. Introduction to artificial intelligence applications and massive data processing (*Big Data*). Use of shared digital spaces and virtual disks for the storage and sharing of information.
- Integration of telecommunications in digital control systems; Internet of things with the different elements, communications and control, through practical application to respond to personal or collective needs.
- Design, construction and control of simple physical or simulated robots for the development of real or fictitious tasks.

**Sustainable technology**

- Selection of materials and design of processes, products and technological systems for environmental, economic and social sustainability.
- Justification of energy as a key technological factor of sustainable development. Energy efficiency, responsible consumption and renewable energies.
- Search, application and design of energy saving strategies in buildings. Analysis of bioclimatic and sustainable architecture in the reduction of environmental impact both locally and globally.
- Analysis and evaluation of the sustainable mobility of the different means of public or private transport.
- Creation of open learning communities, promotion of technological volunteerism and the implementation of community service projects with an active commitment both locally and globally.
